Description

Active MEK1 and MEK2, phosphorylated on two serines of their activation loop, phosphorylate ERK1 and ERK2 on a threonine and a tyrosine two residues apart in the activation loop (Thr202 and Tyr204 in ERK1, Thr185 and Tyr187 in ERK2), and both phosphorylations are needed for ERK activity [1]. MEK does not add the two phosphates in one encounter: it phosphorylates one site, usually the tyrosine, releases the monophosphorylated ERK and must bind it again to phosphorylate the threonine [2, 3]. This two-collision mechanism makes the response of ERK to MEK steeper than that of a single phosphorylation [2].

References

  2. Ferrell JE, Bhatt RR. Mechanistic studies of the dual phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase. J Biol Chem. 1997;272(30):19008-16. PMID: 9228083. doi: 10.1074/jbc.272.30.19008.
  3. Burack WR, Sturgill TW. The activating dual phosphorylation of MAPK by MEK is nonprocessive. Biochemistry. 1997;36(20):5929-33. PMID: 9166761. doi: 10.1021/bi970535d.
